changes_made.explanation: Consolidated methods and criteria descriptions. Paper uses GPT-4 as LLM judge with specific prompting techniques to evaluate statement faithfulness and type.

guideline: Multi-stage annotation protocol: identify statement type (factual/cognitive), then assess faithfulness using rational/grounded/unequivocal criteria
- The guidelines for annotators to assess cognitive statements are summarized as follows: 1. Identifying Statements Types... 2. Assessing Faithfulness...
- Identify statement type, then assess faithfulness using the three criteria: Rational, Grounded, Unequivocal.

- Annotators undergo comprehensive training to ensure they fully understand the annotation standards outlined in Section 2.2. They must also pass a test annotation set before beginning formal annotation.

changes_made.explanation: Normalized criteria capitalization and consolidated guideline into a concise description. Added missing categories (Misleading/Speculative/Reliable) that are part of the final classification system.

overall_notes: Paper focuses on NLG evaluation for dialogue generation, specifically assessing faithfulness hallucinations in factual vs cognitive statements. The extraction was generally accurate but needed normalization and consolidation of similar items. Paper includes both human evaluation and LLM-as-judge approaches.
